$description:
Lolly starter brand tokens — the OKLCH-native DTCG document shipped with the blank lolly-start profile. It doubles as the reference example of the brand token contract (plans/brand-token-contract.md): three ramps + a spectrum in a shared 'base' set, and per-theme semantic slots that alias into them. Every $value is a CSS oklch() string (L%, chroma, hue); anything needing hex goes through the engine's colorToHex.

Colours come from Evil Martians' Harmony palette (https://github.com/evilmartians/harmony, MIT) — no tooling, just the values. Harmony is an 11-step ladder (50..950) where chroma follows a fixed bell peaking at 500 and per-hue lightness is tuned so APCA contrast is equal across hues at a given step and MIRRORED about the 500 pivot (50<->950, 100<->900, 200<->800, 300<->700, 400<->600). The contract wants 9 steps, so we take the mirrored subset that drops the 200/800 pair: the lolly ramp is then mirror-symmetric in its own right (1<->9, 2<->8, 3<->7, 4<->6) with step 5 sitting exactly on the Harmony 500 pivot. Practical payoff: any step and its mirror are interchangeable between the light and dark themes, and the primary/secondary/neutral ramps are contrast-matched step for step.

Anchor: primary = Harmony Indigo (hue 260), neutrals = Harmony Slate (hue 275, so grays lean toward the primary), supporting accent = Harmony Teal (hue 160). Scheme duo. Replace wholesale via the #/start wizard or 'npm run ingest:brand'.

primary.$description: The brand ramp — Harmony's Indigo (hue 260) at its native chroma bell. Step 5 is the Harmony 500 pivot itself (#6ca6ff); steps 4 and 6 are the mirrored pair either side of it, which is why the light and dark themes can use them interchangeably.

1.$description: Deep brand ink — on-primary in both themes, near-black brand fills

2.$description: Dark emphasis fills and hover states on light surfaces

3.$description: Strong accent for small text on light surfaces — 5.3:1 on surface (Harmony 700, APCA 77)

4.$description: THE light-theme primary — 3.7:1 on surface, carries step 1 as its text at 4.9:1 (Harmony 600, APCA 65)

5.$description: The Harmony 500 pivot — the ramp's most saturated step, for large brand shapes

6.$description: THE dark-theme primary — 9.4:1 on the dark surface (Harmony 400, step 4's mirror)

8.$description: Pale tint — washes and large decorative shapes

neutral.$description: Quiet grays from Harmony's Slate (hue 275, chroma held flat at 0.024), so 'gray' UI still leans toward the indigo primary instead of going dead neutral. Surfaces, text and hairlines all come from here.

2.$description: Raised dark surface and dark-theme hairlines (1.4:1 on the dark surface)

3.$description: Light-theme muted text — 5.3:1 on the light surface (Harmony 700, APCA 77)

4.$description: Mid-dark gray — secondary icons and rules on light surfaces

5.$description: The Harmony 500 pivot — disabled states, placeholder text

6.$description: Lifted gray — secondary icons on dark surfaces

7.$description: Dark-theme muted text and light-theme hairlines (11.7:1 on the dark surface, 1.5:1 on the light one)

8.$description: Subtle fills — cards, wells, input backgrounds

secondary.$description: The supporting accent — Harmony's Teal (hue 160), 100° off the primary so it reads as a genuinely different colour rather than a tint of it. Harmony's per-hue lightness tuning means it lands at the same APCA contrast as the primary step for step, so the two can be swapped without re-checking legibility.

3.$description: Strong supporting accent on light surfaces — 5.3:1 on surface

5.$description: The Harmony 500 pivot — the ramp's most saturated step

6.$description: THE dark-theme secondary — 9.5:1 on the dark surface

spectrum.$description:
The full Harmony chromatic wheel — all seventeen families at step 600, the level Harmony tunes to APCA 65 on white, so every hue here is equally readable against the light surface and equally weighted against its neighbours. Hues are Harmony's own, not nudged toward the primary: the set is meant to be discriminable first, on-brand second.

Order is deliberate and is NOT the hue wheel. Chart tools (chart-creator, d3) walk color.spectrum.* in document order to assign series colours, so a wheel ordering would hand a two-series chart red and orange. These are ordered by greedy maximum hue separation, seeded with the original six so existing charts keep their palette: the first eight stay at least 30 degrees apart, degrading gracefully after that. Append new entries at the end rather than re-sorting.

semantic.$description: The seven semantic slots for the light look (the default theme — light is first in $themes). Every slot aliases a ramp step. WCAG 2.1 ratios were computed against the resolved sRGB values and honor the contract floors: text >= 7.0, muted >= 3.0, on-primary >= 4.5, edge >= 1.3.

primary.$description: The brand colour — Harmony Indigo 600, 3.7:1 on surface

on-primary.$description: Text/icons on primary — the deep brand ink, 4.9:1 on primary (paper only reaches 3.7:1 here, so the dark ramp end wins)

secondary.$description: Supporting accent for fills and badges — 3.7:1 on surface

semantic.$description: The seven semantic slots for the dark look — the light theme reflected through Harmony's mirror pairs rather than hand-retuned. Same contract floors, same computed-ratio discipline.

primary.$description: The brand colour lifted for dark surfaces — step 4's Harmony mirror, 9.4:1 on surface

on-primary.$description: Text/icons on primary — the same deep brand ink as the light theme, 9.4:1 on the lifted primary

secondary.$description: Supporting accent lifted to match — 9.5:1 on surface

muted.$description: Secondary foreground — step 3's mirror, 11.7:1 on surface

edge.$description: Hairlines and borders — 1.4:1 on surface, matching the light theme's 1.5:1 hairline in perceived faintness
